summary: Jesus and His disciples baptize in Judea; when John’s disciples complain that all are going to Him, John rejoices: “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
key_insight: John’s disciples brought him a complaint: “all are coming to Him!” John heard the same news as the fulfillment of his joy. The friend of the bridegroom is glad when the bride goes to the groom.
story: After His conversation with Nicodemus in Jerusalem, Jesus and His disciples went out into the Judean countryside. He stayed there with them and baptized.
John the Baptist was still at work too, baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there, and people kept coming to be baptized. John had not yet been thrown into prison.

A dispute arose between some of John’s disciples and the Jews about purification. Then John’s disciples came to him with news that troubled them: “Rabbi, He who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified,” they said, “behold, He is baptizing, and all are coming to Him!”

John answered, “A man can receive nothing unless it has been given to him from heaven.” He reminded them of his own words: “You yourselves bear me witness, that I said, ‘I am not the Christ,’ but, ‘I have been sent before Him.’ ”

Then he described himself as the bridegroom’s friend. The bride belongs to the bridegroom. His friend stands by, listens, and rejoices greatly when he hears the bridegroom’s voice. “Therefore this joy of mine is fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.”

John went on to say why. “He who comes from above is above all.” He speaks the words of God, for God does not give the Spirit by measure. “The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into His hand. He who believes in the Son has everlasting life; and he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him.”

scene.label: Aenon near Salim
scene.text: Aenon means springs. Its exact site is uncertain. Some place it in the Jordan Valley south of Beth-shan, others in the hills east of Shechem in Samaria. John chose it for one plain reason: there was much water there.

scene.label: Purification
scene.text: Jews of the time practiced many ritual washings (John 2:6; Mark 7:3–4). Two baptizers working at once, John and Jesus’ disciples, raised questions about what each washing meant. John does not record the details of the argument, only where it led.

scene.label: The friend of the bridegroom
scene.text: At a Jewish wedding the groom’s close friend helped arrange the marriage and the celebration. His task was to bring bride and groom together, never to win the bride for himself. The prophets pictured God as Israel’s bridegroom (Isaiah 62:5; Hosea 2:19–20).

scene.label: Who did the baptizing?
scene.text: John 3:22 says Jesus baptized; John 4:2 adds that Jesus Himself did not baptize, but His disciples. They baptized under His authority. This was probably a baptism of repentance like John’s, not yet baptism in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19).

witnesses.john: John alone tells of these months when Jesus and John the Baptist were at work side by side, and he notes that John “had not yet been thrown into prison.” The other Gospels begin Jesus’ public work in Galilee after that arrest. These are the Baptist’s last words in John’s Gospel, and they end where the whole book aims: believing in the Son and having life (John 20:31).

seeing.reveals: Jesus is the Bridegroom who comes from above. The Father loves Him, has given all things into His hand, and gives Him the Spirit without measure. Life or wrath turns on how a person responds to Him.
seeing.living: John’s disciples measured success by the crowds and felt the loss. John measured it by the Bridegroom’s voice and called it joy. When another servant’s work grows and yours shrinks, the real question is whether Jesus is being heard.
seeing.ponder: Whose growing fruitfulness do you find hard to celebrate, and what would change if you heard it as the Bridegroom’s voice?

preaching.big_idea: Joy is fullest when Jesus increases and we decrease.
outline: A servant who knows his place (27–28)
A Son who is above all (31–36)
preaching.watch_for: John 3:30 is the hinge of the passage. The NKJV keeps John speaking to the end, but many think the Gospel writer’s own reflection begins at verse 31. Either way, verses 31–36 explain why John must decrease: the One from above is above all.
